one_liner: Double-precision SIMD Mersenne Twister in C that emits IEEE 754 doubles directly; about 1.6x MT19937 for bulk uniform doubles.
what_it_does: A Mersenne-Twister-family generator (Saito and Matsumoto) whose 128-bit recursion writes the 52 mantissa bits of a double in [1,2) with the exponent preset, so a uniform double costs one state word and, for [0,1), one subtraction. The C API is struct based (dsfmt_t plus dsfmt_init_gen_rand, dsfmt_genrand_close_open, dsfmt_fill_array_close_open and variants for the four interval conventions) with a parallel dsfmt_gv_* set on a global state. It is not a drop-in for std::mt19937 or MT19937: the output stream, period parameters and integer API differ.
how_it_is_fast: The state is an array of 128-bit words updated with a single SSE2 (or AltiVec) recursion of shifts, a 32-bit shuffle, XORs and a mask (do_recursion in dSFMT-common.h), producing two doubles per step with no tempering. Because the exponent bits are fixed by the recursion, no integer-to-float conversion is needed; MT19937 by contrast spends two tempered 32-bit outputs per 53-bit double (randomgen's mt19937_next_double), which is where most of the measured uniform-double gain comes from. fill_array_* writes a whole block straight into the caller's 16-byte-aligned array, the authors' recommended fast path.
when_to_use: Monte Carlo code that consumes large blocks of uniform doubles and can call dsfmt_fill_array_close_open on an aligned buffer of at least 382 elements (MEXP 19937).
Reproducing results of software that used dSFMT, such as Julia's MersenneTwister (the default RNG before Julia 1.7) or randomgen's DSFMT bit generator.

Projects that want an MT-family generator with a very long period (2^19937-1 by default, up to 2^216091-1 via DSFMT_MEXP) and jump-ahead (the repo's jump/ directory) but faster double output than MT19937.
Plain C99 code bases on x86-64 or POWER that prefer a small BSD-3-Clause source drop (dSFMT.c plus headers) over a library dependency.
when_not_to_use: Integer streams: randomgen's own table shows DSFMT slower than MT19937 for Uint32 (2.8 vs 2.5 ns) and equal for Uint64 (4.2 vs 4.2 ns, each uint64 consumes two dSFMT outputs); the header itself says dsfmt_genrand_uint32 'is slower than SFMT, only for convenience usage'.

New designs with no compatibility need: randomgen's performance page recommends against every Mersenne Twister variant, and SFC64, Xoshiro256 and PCG64DXSM are as fast or faster for doubles there with tiny state.

Many parallel streams or per-task generators: the state is 192 128-bit words (about 3 KB) at MEXP 19937, the large-state cost Julia's 1.7 release notes cite for moving its default to per-task Xoshiro256++.

ARM64 or other non-SSE2, non-AltiVec targets on the master branch: the portable C path is used there; AVX2, AVX-512 and NEON code exists only on the unreleased 'experimental' branch (ver. 2.2.99, 2025-07-15), whose PR notes AVX-512 'still doesn't run correctly'.
Anything security related: it is a linear generator and not cryptographically secure.

integration.dependencies: none (C standard library; emmintrin.h when HAVE_SSE2 is defined)
integration.min_toolchain: C99 (Makefile uses -std=c99 -O3); GCC, Clang, MSVC and Borland code paths present
integration.platforms: any IEEE 754 platform; SIMD path only for x86 SSE2 (-msse2 -DHAVE_SSE2) and PowerPC AltiVec (-DHAVE_ALTIVEC); big-endian non-GCC needs DSFMT_BIG_ENDIAN
integration.thread_safety: one dsfmt_t per thread is safe; the dsfmt_gv_* functions share the global dsfmt_global_data and are not thread safe (CHANGE-LOG 2.1.1 fixed SSE2 constant initialisation that broke under OpenMP)

gotchas: fill_array preconditions (size even, size >= dsfmt_get_min_array_size(), array 16-byte aligned on the SIMD build) are enforced only by assert(), and the shipped Makefile compiles with -DNDEBUG, so a short, odd-sized or misaligned buffer is silently undefined behaviour rather than an error.
fill_array_* and genrand_* calls must not be mixed on one state without re-initialising, per the dSFMT.c documentation.

DSFMT_MEXP must be identical for dSFMT.c and every caller; a mismatch makes dsfmt_init_gen_rand print 'DSFMT_MEXP doesn't match with dSFMT.c' and call exit(1) from inside the library. Leaving it undefined triggers a #warning and defaults to 19937.

SIMD is opt-in: without -DHAVE_SSE2 the code compiles the scalar path with no warning, and doubles have 52-bit resolution (multiples of 2^-52), one bit less than MT19937's 53-bit doubles in NumPy and randomgen.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick dSFMT over SFMT when the output you need is doubles (SFMT is the better MT variant for 32/64-bit integers and ties dSFMT on randomgen's uniform row at 2.5 ns); pick it over randomgen's SFC64 or Xoshiro256 only when you need the dSFMT stream itself or MT-family period guarantees, since those match or beat it on the same table with a tiny state, and prefer VMT19937 when the standard MT19937 stream must be reproduced with AVX2 or AVX-512.
verified_claims_summary: randomgen's performance table (Python timeit through NumPy's Generator, 25,000 values per call, best of 10x100, Intel Cascade Lake at 3.1 GHz, Linux) gives DSFMT 2.5 ns per uniform double against randomgen's MT19937 4.0 ns (about 1.6x, derived from page data) and NumPy RandomState 5.2 ns, with integer, exponential and gamma rows equal or slower; it measures randomgen's vendored dSFMT.c built with -DHAVE_SSE2, not this repository, and the compiler, version and flags behind the table (last edited 2020-2023) are not stated.
status_note: Stale but stable: master last changed 2025-05-19 (PR #7), the code base is ver. 2.2.x from 2011-2020 with no tagged releases, one open issue (#9, seeding from another RNG), and a 2025 AVX2/AVX-512/NEON contribution parked on an experimental branch; BSD-3-Clause and small enough to vendor.
